Shingō field manual · section 01
Shape alphabet12 primitives · one angle (45°, rising "/") · flat print · no rounding
A · Cut plate

Chamfers at top-left and bottom-right only, at 6, 12 or 24 pt. Buttons, keys, cards.

B · Tag

One cut, bottom-right. The coral signal slab and every bar's free end.

C · Nested bar

A solid print bar with a slot cut in, ending in a 45° tag. Progress and scrubbers.

D · Slash

A "/" parallelogram. Steps, cells and stripes are all slashes in a row.

E · Hazard

Slashes between two rules. The divider between masthead and body.

F · Notch

A hairline frame with its label tab cut into the corner, like a drawing's title block.

G · Hard X

Two crossed bars, square-cut ends. Solid for done, outline for rest, coral for now.

H · Diamond

A square turned 45° with an off-centre hole. The mark, blips and bullets.

I · Chevrons

Nested "^" with broken left arms. The one large artwork: hero, key art, paywall.

J · Brackets

Four L corners around anything that is a viewport: scopes, spectra, maps, scenes.

K · Cell run

Slashes that fill up. Levels, rounds and caps.

L · Wedge

A 45° triangle of coral in a corner. Poster screens only.

SG·§02Rev 261102 / 08

Screens

iPhone 390 × 844 pt · one grammar, two tiers · placeholder brand "AXIOM"

Shingō field manual · section 02
01Two inks

Everything is print on ground: solid shapes in the print ink with text knocked out, or outlines. No third tone. Coral is the only extra ink.

02One grammar

Masthead, one hero, a divider, the body, the imprint. Each screen sits on one backdrop composition from the shape alphabet. Poster screens compose freely.

03One angle

Every diagonal rises left to right at 45°: corner cuts (top-left and bottom-right), hazard stripes, cells, bands and the stripe field. No tilts, textures or shadows.

04Three sizes

One face, three weights and a stencil, all cut like the plates. Shingo Grid Heavy sets display 40 and up, titles 32 and big figures; Bold sets subheads and inline wordmarks; Medium sets labels in caps; the stencil cut sets serials and stamps. Body is Anybody, telemetry is mono.

05One signal

Coral marks one block or one primary action per screen, plus the latest or active state. Switches turn on in print, not coral.

06Tag and aside

Japanese lives in the masthead tag or a seal. French lives in the span rule. Each appears once at most.

Content motifsshapes taken from each screen's subject · same rules as the alphabet
Lock tumblers

Passcode. Six pin stacks; entered digits align on the shear line, the latest pin in coral.

Postage and cancel

Inbox. A perforated stamp with a square postmark and cancel bars.

DIP switch bank

Settings. Eight switches print the config word; the last one changed is coral.

Wind barbs

Conditions. Meteorological barbs for the next six hours: lines are 10 kt, a pennant is 50.

Packet flow

Transfer. Account to person as slash packets; the one in flight is coral.

Cut fingerprint

Credential. Ridges drawn as broken cut-corner loops.

Compass rose

Route. Eight points from diamonds; north in coral.

Level meters

Player. Left and right cell columns; the peak cell runs hot.

Security microtext

Wallet. Repeating micro type printed under the card, like a banknote.

Big numerals for timers, speed, balances and counters, set in Shingo Grid figures, each in a fixed cell so live values never jump. Any digit can light coral.

Cells slanted at the system's 45°, like a hazard stripe that fills up. For levels, rounds and caps. The last cell can run hot.

Up to four equal-width 45° slim tracks in one row, keyed by 5×5 square pips in coral-harmonized telemetry inks (jade, cerulean, marigold, iris). Threshold alerts tint only the readout text in signal coral so every series keeps its hue.

Three languages

english · 日本語 · français

Shingō field manual · section 08
EN

English runs the interface

Every action, label and number. If someone has to read it to use the app, it's in English.

Protected
日本語

Japanese adds texture

Vertical captions along edges, seal stamps and outlined display kanji. Use one Japanese moment per screen at most. It is never the only label on a control.

認証受信箱圏外
Fr.

French is the aside

Italic footnotes, dates, taglines and pull quotes. Use it once per screen at most, usually in the quietest spot.

« celui qu'on n'entend pas »
×3

All three only once

Stack the same line in all three languages in one place only: the lock screen, splash or about page. Repeating the stack elsewhere weakens it.
